corrected_classifications.reason: DELETE is not defensible. It is already outside the product dependency graph (crates/client-core/Cargo.toml has no kama-integration entry), so it cannot mislead a build; it is not dead (it is the live harness for the A2/DR-CS campaign tests and examples); and crates/kama-engine/src/cold_rx_state.rs:5,164,269 designate it the INSTANCE/LIFECYCLE owner of GlobalColdLedger, so deletion orphans those types. The genuine defect is the misleading '//! A2-F0 İSKELETİ — ReceiverHost: ürün-alıcı COMPOSITION-ROOT' header at receiver_host.rs:1, which is a one-line doc correction. KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL with a required doc fix, plus the deferred port of the cold-ledger bounds into runtime.rs, matches the evidence.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Sender block accumulation + deterministic block/ESI assignment
corrected_classifications.reason: SHIP is not defensible as filed. SHIP requires 'required for v1' AND correct-by-architecture; this mechanism violates a NORMATİF KARAR-VERİLDİ clause of the authority spec on every block it forms. specs/fec-core-tdd-v3.0.md:169-171 states `block-sınırı message/chunk-tabanlıdır. Bir-FEC-block birden-fazla-application-message-İÇEREMEZ ... cross-message-block-YASAK`, and crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1275-1277 derives block membership purely from `id % k_shape` with no message_id term — under the product default (fragmenter OFF, runtime.rs:188) a K=8 block spans 8 distinct application messages. The accumulation code is wired and works, so this is 'spec-required but incorrectly connected', which is the WIRE bucket, not SHIP-with-a-note. Downgrading also keeps it adjacent to the partial-block WIRE record, which is the same §3/§6 defect family (both stem from close-on-K-only).

Label retained but conditionally: the classification's own clause 'not secretly needed for v1 claims' is currently violated, and that must be recorded rather than left in notes. All three client-core FEC e2e proofs use manual_r Some(4) (crates/client-core/tests/runtime_e2e.rs:387,483,554) and the sole Controller-mode end-to-end exercise lives in a non-CI example (crates/client-core/examples/fec_arm_compare.rs:300), so every 'FEC recovers erased units on the product path' claim rests on the experimental arm. KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL is correct as to default state (crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:199 fec: None) but the record must carry the dependency, and closing it requires a Controller-mode e2e test, not a relabel.
